mappings.note: Two pots, one sealed with oil, to test whether seeds need air. Recognising a controlled investigation and predicting its result, LO-108.
Assertion-reason: plants are living BECAUSE they grow, respond and reproduce. Requires the living/non-living distinction on its properties, LO-106.

Which processes plants and animals share -- nutrition and respiration, but not locomotion. A differentiation of the two groups on their properties, LO-106. The stem retains only the last of the three numbered items.
Shoots emerging from a farmer's field is germination. Naming the process from an account of it, LO-110.
The seed's outer covering is the seed coat. Naming a structure, LO-105.
Leaf pores are stomata. Naming a structure, LO-105.
Producing new individuals of one's kind is reproduction. Naming a life process, LO-110.
Name the insectivorous plant -- Drosera. Identifying an organism, LO-105.
The jelly-like egg cluster is spawn. Naming a stage from its appearance, LO-105.
Who built the crescograph. The device and its maker; LO-113 covers constructing an instrument, and no LO reaches biography.
The stage after the egg is the larva. Ordering the life-cycle stage set, LO-107.
Plants excrete excess water and minerals as droplets. Explaining a life process in plants, LO-110.
The prompt for a response is a stimulus. Naming the concept, LO-105.
Removing waste from the body is excretion. Naming a life process, LO-110.
Taking air in and out is breathing. Naming a life process, LO-110.
Water softens the seed coat. The mechanism by which a condition acts, LO-109.
The root grows downwards. Naming a part by its behaviour, LO-105.
After the tailed tadpole comes the tadpole with legs. Ordering the life-cycle stage set, LO-107.
The plant folding its leaves on touch is touch-me-not. LO-110's 'movements in plants' example.
Silk moth larvae secrete silk fibre. Identifying an organism by what it produces, LO-105.
Tails are what let tadpoles swim. A structure tied to a function its habitat demands, LO-109.
Name a disease female mosquitoes transmit -- malaria. The health reason behind the chapter's call to clear standing water, LO-115.
The final stage of a plant's life cycle is death. Ordering the life-cycle stage set, LO-107.
Climbers wind around objects. LO-110's 'movements in plants' example.
After the egg comes the embryo in a frog's cycle. Ordering the stage set, LO-107.
Urine is an excretion product. Naming an instance of a life process, LO-110.
Which scientist experimented on plant responses -- J.C. Bose. His crescograph is the device, so LO-113; no LO covers biography.
A seed becoming a sprout is germination. Naming a life process, LO-110.
Which condition germination does NOT need -- light. The conclusion of the germination investigation, LO-108.
Why standing water must not be allowed -- it breeds disease-carrying mosquitoes. A protective habit for the surroundings, LO-115.
How a car differs from a living being although both move. An explicit differentiation on the properties of life, LO-106.
How plants move without travelling -- flowers opening, Drosera hairs, climbers winding. LO-110's 'movements in plants' example set.
What Drosera's sticky hair tips are for -- trapping insects it feeds on. A structure related to how the plant obtains nutrition, LO-109.
Why respiration is essential -- it converts food into usable energy. Explaining a life process, LO-110.
Excretion in plants, seen as droplets on grass and rose leaves. Explaining a life process in plants, LO-110.
What a stimulus is, with a response from an animal and from a plant. Explaining responses in both, LO-110.
Why reproduction is necessary -- continuity of the species. Explaining a life process, LO-110.
The three conditions most seeds need to germinate. The conclusion of the germination investigation, LO-108.
How water helps germination -- it softens the coat and enables the embryo to develop. The mechanism by which a condition acts, LO-109.
Why air matters -- seeds draw it from the spaces between soil particles. The mechanism by which a condition acts, LO-109.
Whether light always blocks germination -- Coleus and Petunia need it. Sorting seeds into those needing light and those not, LO-107.
The general growth direction of root and shoot. Explaining a growth movement, LO-110.
What a plant's life cycle is. Explaining a process, LO-110.
The four mosquito stages named. The life-cycle stage set, LO-107.
How kerosene disrupts the cycle -- the film cuts larvae off from air. The causal mechanism, LO-109.
What tadpoles are and where they live early on. Identifying a stage by its features and habitat, LO-105.
The transition from tadpole to froglet. Explaining a developmental process, LO-110.
How adult frogs differ from froglets in habitat and features. An explicit differentiation of two stages, LO-106.
Why the dramatic changes in mosquito and frog life cycles matter -- survival and continuity. The reason behind a pattern, LO-109.
The seed coat's role -- softened by water so the embryo can emerge. A structure's function in a process, LO-109.
Why larvae and pupae surface repeatedly -- they need air to respire. The cause of an observed behaviour, LO-109.
What 'dead' means -- no life characteristics despite resources. Explaining a life process, LO-110.
How soil air spaces help -- supplying air and letting roots expand. The mechanism by which a condition acts, LO-109.
What spawn is -- white jelly-like egg mass at the pond edge. Identifying a stage from its appearance and where it occurs, LO-105.
Discuss all the characteristics separating living from non-living. An explicit differentiation at essay length, LO-106.
How stationary plants still move, with examples. LO-110's own 'movements in plants' example set, at essay length.
J.C. Bose's crescograph and what it recorded about plant responses to light, heat, electricity and gravity. Constructing an instrument and explaining its working, LO-113.
The germination conditions AND why each matters. The mechanisms, not merely the list, so LO-109.
DESIGN an experiment on whether sunlight is needed for germination, with a control and an observation window. Planning an investigation, LO-108.
Response to stimuli explained with an animal and a plant example. Explaining responses in both, LO-110.
